report.topicTitle: 3-layer memory: facts table tracks each fact as a discrete, individually addressable record
report.summary: This topic specifies the core of a 3-layer memory design for the Auspicion Suite: a **facts table** in which every extracted fact is stored as a discrete, individually addressable record, rather than as an opaque blob of conversation history. It builds directly on the `mem0-chat-extraction` dependency, which supplies the extraction pipeline that turns raw chat logs into structured facts. The design separates three layers — (1) raw chat/event capture, (2) extraction into discrete facts, and (3) a queryable/recall layer — so that each fact carries its own identity, provenance, confidence, and lifecycle. Because each fact is individually addressable, the system can update, invalidate, merge, or delete a single fact without rewriting the whole memory, and can cite the exact source chat message that produced it. This is the "facts as first-class objects" pattern: facts are not incidental byproducts of a conversation but durable, addressable knowledge units. The design is a Level-2 concern (a core architectural layer) and is a prerequisite for the higher-level memory features (graph memory, entity resolution, recall) in the suite's tools.
report.state-of-the-art:
The current state of the art in AI-agent memory has moved decisively away from "dump the whole transcript into context" toward structured, layered memory. The dominant open-source reference is **mem0** ([mem0ai/mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0)), which organizes memory into three types — **facts**, **entities**, and **insights** — and optionally a **memory graph** that links them ([docs.mem0.ai memory-types](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-types), [graph-memory](https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/features/graph-memory)). mem0's pipeline is: extract → update → add, where new information is compared against existing memory and only genuinely new facts are added ([how-it-works](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/how-it-works)). This is exactly the "extract facts from chat logs" mechanism that the `mem0-chat-extraction` dependency provides.

The "three-layer AI memory architecture" is a widely taught pattern: **storage → injection → recall** ([MindStudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/three-layer-ai-memory-architecture), [Claude Code memory system](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/claude-code-memory-system-storage-injection-recall)). The facts table sits in the storage layer and is the unit that injection and recall operate on.

The most relevant recent research is **"Facts as First-Class Objects: Knowledge Objects for Persistent LLM Memory"** ([arXiv 2603.17781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17781v1), [ar5iv HTML](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2603.17781)): it argues facts should be treated as first-class, individually addressable knowledge objects rather than embedded in unstructured text, enabling targeted update and invalidation. Related work on **schema-grounded memory** ([arXiv 2604.27906](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27906)) shows that iterative, schema-aware extraction produces more reliable, addressable memory than unstructured recall. The **CortexDB five-memory-layers** model ([CortexDB docs](https://cortexdb.ai/docs/concepts/layers)) and **Cloudflare Agent Memory** ([how it works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-memory/concepts/how-agent-memory-works/)) are additional production references for layered, addressable memory stores. The **memorant** project ([tier4research/memorant](https://github.com/tier4research/memorant)) is a research implementation of layered memory. The consensus: discrete, addressable fact records with provenance and confidence are the current best practice for durable agent memory.
report.key-concepts-glossary:
- **3-layer memory**: A memory architecture split into (1) raw capture/event log, (2) extraction into structured facts, and (3) recall/injection. Also described as storage → injection → recall ([MindStudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/three-layer-ai-memory-architecture)).
- **Facts table**: The storage layer's core table where each extracted fact is one row — a discrete, individually addressable record with its own ID, content, provenance, confidence, and lifecycle state.
- **Individually addressable record**: A fact that can be read, updated, invalidated, merged, or deleted by its own identifier without touching other records or rewriting the whole memory.
- **mem0-chat-extraction**: The dependency that extracts structured facts from raw chat logs, feeding the facts table. In mem0 terms this is the "extract" stage of the extract → update → add pipeline ([how-it-works](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/how-it-works)).
- **Fact / entity / insight**: mem0's three memory types — facts are discrete statements, entities are named objects, insights are higher-level inferences ([memory-types](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-types)).
- **Memory graph**: An optional layer linking facts, entities, and insights into a queryable graph ([graph-memory](https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/features/graph-memory)).
- **Provenance**: The source chat message(s) from which a fact was extracted; enables citation and audit.
- **Confidence / recency**: Per-fact metadata used to rank and filter facts at recall time.
- **Facts as first-class objects**: The principle that facts are durable, addressable knowledge units, not incidental byproducts of conversation ([arXiv 2603.17781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17781v1)).
- **Injection**: The layer that selects and inserts relevant facts into the model's context at query time.
- **Recall**: The retrieval layer that queries the facts table (and graph) to answer questions or ground generation.
report.implementation-guide:
Implement the facts table as the storage layer of a 3-layer memory, fed by `mem0-chat-extraction`.

**1. Schema (facts table).** Each row is a discrete, addressable record with at least: `fact_id` (stable UUID), `content` (canonical fact text), `source_chat_id` + `source_message_id` (provenance), `confidence` (0–1), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `last_seen_at`, `status` (active | superseded | invalidated), `entity_ids` (links to the entity layer), and `embedding` (vector for recall). Keep the schema normalized so a fact is addressable by `fact_id` alone.

**2. Extraction pipeline (from mem0-chat-extraction).** On each new chat message: (a) run the extraction step to produce candidate facts; (b) compare each candidate against existing facts (dedup/merge); (c) add genuinely new facts, update changed facts, and mark contradicted facts as superseded — mirroring mem0's extract → update → add ([how-it-works](https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/how-it-works)). Record provenance on every write.

**3. Addressability operations.** Expose CRUD by `fact_id`: `get_fact(id)`, `update_fact(id, ...)`, `invalidate_fact(id)`, `merge_facts(id_a, id_b)`. Never rewrite whole memory; always operate on the single record. This is the "facts as first-class objects" requirement ([arXiv 2603.17781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17781v1)).

**4. Recall/injection layer.** At query time, retrieve candidate facts by vector similarity + recency + confidence, filter by status=active, and inject the top-k into context. Optionally build a memory graph over facts/entities for relational recall ([graph-memory](https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/features/graph-memory)).

**5. Lifecycle & consistency.** Use schema-aware extraction for reliability ([arXiv 2604.27906](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27906)). Handle contradictions by superseding rather than deleting (preserve history). Provide an audit view keyed by provenance so any fact can be traced to its source chat message.

**6. Testing.** Unit-test each addressability operation (get/update/invalidate/merge) in isolation; test extraction→table writes with provenance; test recall ranking; test contradiction handling. Follow the suite's TDD gate (red → green) and the trio (test, typecheck, build).
report.per-project-application-notes:
- **Familiar**: The facts table is the primary memory store for the assistant's long-term knowledge of the user. Each fact (e.g., "user prefers email over phone") is individually addressable so a single correction updates one record without rewriting the profile. Recall injects the top relevant facts into each conversation.
- **Astrographer**: Store extracted astrological/observational facts (birth data, chart readings, user-reported events) as discrete addressable records with provenance to the source chat. Enables targeted correction of a single chart datum and cross-referencing facts across readings.
- **Incanter**: Use the facts table to persist extracted spell/ritual/incantation facts and user preferences. Individual addressability lets a user amend one ritual detail without losing the rest of the memory; provenance ties each fact to the chat where it was learned.
- **Horoscope**: Persist per-user horoscope-relevant facts (birth date/time, sign, recurring concerns) as discrete records. Recall filters by recency and confidence so daily horoscopes are grounded in the latest, most reliable facts; a single fact can be invalidated when a user corrects it.
- **Solomon**: Store extracted judgment/decision facts and user constraints as individually addressable records. Each fact carries provenance and status so a superseded ruling can be marked invalid without deleting history, and recall injects only active, high-confidence facts.
- **Augur**: Persist extracted predictions/outcomes and user context as discrete facts. Addressability enables outcome tracking — a prediction fact can be updated to "confirmed/refuted" by ID — and recall grounds future predictions in the most recent, highest-confidence facts.
